quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
You may not pass.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A good rule for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases collision risk. If you drive faster than others, you will keep passing. Drive with traffic flow within the speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can fully cross the tracks without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can fully cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough space to fully cross the tracks before driving on them. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Slam on the brakes to get them to back off.
Change lanes or slowly down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slowly down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often to notice tailgaters or fast-approaching vehicles. If someone is following too closely, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when vehicles follow too closely.

questions.question: When another driver is passing your car, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
questions.explanation: Stay right when another driver begins to pass on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them return to the right lane safely.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
Certain turns are allowed only from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Drivers in both lanes must merge smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane sign. HOV lanes are for buses and cars with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a sharp turn ahead and tells you to reduce speed.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reaction time becomes slower.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You become less alert.
You calm down and focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to see from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full lane width to operate safely. They are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other motor vehicles.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park in certain places, including on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. You can only cross them to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, scooter riders, or skateboarders if the other lane is clear.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Both directions can pass.
No passing is allowed.
You can pass at the top of a hill.
You can pass during the day only.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic is moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting danger and acting to prevent accidents.
Passing other cars to get ahead in traffic.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting danger and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes caused by reckless, careless, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if your car breaks down on a highway?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Honk at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down, turn on your hazard flashers. Move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know you need help.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to look.
Turn your head and look out the back window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the back window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your car before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look out the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season for driving.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other bad conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Driver mistakes
Bad weather
Poor road conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Driver mistakes
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other cars or act unexpectedly. Talk with other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: Anytime.
Only during daylight.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your car to get help.
Go to sleep in your car.
Walk into the road to get attention.
Stay in your car so rescuers can find you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car so rescuers can find you.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car if stranded in a snowstorm. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.
